properties.description:
Implement the organization accepted in completed task 6a. Establish RelationalEngine's public API boundary without redesigning its data model; keep the shared organization checker reusable.

1. Source organization and depth

Rename the system and source folder from RelationEngine to RelationalEngine, updating affected workspace/project paths, imports, tooling and references. Retain the existing @super-app/relational-engine package identity and leave no old-name aliases.

Keep one package and one package.json:
- Systems/DepthN/SystemName/Api/DepthN/SubsystemApiName/
- Systems/DepthN/SystemName/Impl/DepthN/SubsystemImplName/

Api and Impl separate public contracts from private implementation. They do not require matching names, paths or depth numbers. Calculate dependency depth across both halves of the same owning system, retaining the existing recursive depth and cycle rules. For example: an Api/Depth0 contract is used by an Impl/Depth1 implementation, which is used by an Api/Depth2 creation entry point.

2. Readable API and ordinary TypeScript compilation

Author Api in .ts files with explicit function signatures, argument/return types, public methods/properties and comments. Public types belong to Api or declared public dependencies. An API factory can contain a small body that constructs its own implementation and returns the public contract. Concrete classes and operational logic belong to Impl. Prefix interface names with I and use the ordinary name for concrete implementations: IRelationalEngine in Api and RelationalEngine in Impl. Do not add an Implementation suffix.

Use the ordinary TypeScript compiler to produce JavaScript and .d.ts declarations. The declarations retain the public signatures and comments while omitting function bodies. A private implementation must not become the inferred public return type.

Configure package exports once with a wildcard targeting the generated API:
{
  "exports": {
    "./*": {
      "types": "./dist/Api/*.d.ts",
      "import": "./dist/Api/*.js"
    }
  }
}

dist is generated build output. Both targets come from the same authored API module, so independent implementation depths need no per-file package mapping, handwritten duplicate declarations, separate API package or custom binding generator.

3. Access and exposure rules

- Consumers access RelationalEngine through public package entry points, with existing declared-dependency rules.
- Impl can use its own Api and Impl, respecting depth and cycle constraints.
- Api construction/delegation entry points can call their own system's Impl.
- Another system cannot access that Impl directly.
- Api cannot re-export implementation symbols, including through aliases, or expose implementation types through public parameters, returns, properties or inheritance.

Allowed: construct RelationalEngine internally and return IRelationalEngine. Rejected: publicly export the concrete RelationalEngine class or expose it as the return type.

4. Enforcement and verification

Use TypeScript for signature compatibility. Extend the existing organization/boundary checks for access restrictions and public exposure, using resolved symbols and generated API declarations rather than only matching import text. Cover direct source paths, aliases, package exports, re-exports and public type leaks. Restrict public exports to the API output.

Only RelationalEngine adopts the split layout in this task. The shared checker recognizes layout per owning package: paired Api/Impl roots use the new rules; existing DepthN/Subsystem roots retain the current organization rules. Validate each package as one layout and report partial or mixed layouts rather than silently bypassing checks. This requires no hardcoded RelationalEngine exception. Apply privacy according to the target package: a consumer using the existing layout can import RelationalEngine's API but cannot access its Impl. Preserve depth, cycle and declared-dependency checks for both layouts.

Tests remain package-owned; tests requiring private internals belong under Impl, and consumer tests use the public API. Keep tests and test helpers out of public exports. Write API comments, but defer automated documentation-presence checks.

Verify accepted/rejected examples, public package imports, generated declarations and coexistence of both layouts, including imports from unchanged packages and rejection of mixed layouts. Produce actionable file/line findings for offending consumers across the active TheBroccoli, BtrTemplate and PersoTemplate composition. The check must run and report violations without exemptions or exposing internals to make existing consumers pass.

Deliver the RelationalEngine organization and runnable enforcement here, including the impact on systems affected by the rename and Api/Impl split: update imports, contracts, configuration and consumers as needed to keep the active composition working with no boundary violations. Keep unrelated packages in their current organization. The following human review inspects the actual Api folder and its public shape. After approval, task 6c addresses wider adoption of the reviewed API in areas not already affected by this split.

Delivery

Implemented and committed on master: TheBroccoli a0f85487; BtrTemplate 1e11c79; PersoTemplate 4278b28. All three worktrees are clean. The renamed RelationalEngine now has authored public contracts and typed entry points under Api, with concrete code and verification under Impl. The shared checker supports both package layouts and rejects private access, implementation re-exports and public type leaks. Affected consumers and browser package resolution use the new boundary.

Validation: builds, strict types, organization/privacy checks, package/model tests and affected consumer tests passed. Regenerated stale model artifacts and reran the model checks; the planning timing case passed in its focused run after exceeding its budget under concurrent checkpoint load. Browser checkpoint: 398/400 passed; both failed scenarios then passed unchanged in a fresh fixture (3/3 tests). No expectation or timeout was weakened. Reviewed the affected UI screenshots and verified the restarted live application.

Next: the required human API-shape review, followed by broader adoption in 6c only after approval.
properties.title: 6b. Enforce the relational engine public API boundary
